correctness.rationale: The final theorem concerns vector-space-rank-one N=Y⊗f with f,Y nonzero on the six-dimensional n4 Lie algebra a=E12,b=E23,c=E34,d=E13,e=E24,z=E14 and brackets [a,b]=d,[b,c]=e,[a,e]=z,[d,c]=z. Substituting into torsion independently gives the scalar alternating equation f(x)f([Y,y])-f(y)f([Y,x])-f(Y)f([x,y])=0. I constructed all 15 independent pair rows symbolically from these brackets, not from package output. For h=f(z)!=0, rows (d,z),(e,z),(a,z),(c,z),(a,e) force A=C=0,D=-tB/h,E=-sB/h,F=(2st-hv)B/h², and multiplication by h² verifies all 15 equations identically over Z (thus in every characteristic). For h=0 and (s,t)!=(0,0), other rows force B=0,sA=tC, and sD+tE=-(sw+tu)λ with A=tλ,C=sλ; substituting yields only -s and -t times that final relation. For h=s=t=0, all 15 rows vanish. This verifies kernel dimensions 1,3,6 including characteristic two. The projective Segre incidence has irreducible strata of dimensions 5+0=5,4+2=6,2+5=7; the last two are confined to h=0/h=s=t=0 while dimensions preclude containment of larger strata in smaller closures, so they yield precisely three reduced irreducible components; cones add one dimension. Counting nonzero f in each stratum and nonzero Y modulo q-1 yields T(q) and N²=f(Y)N with (q³-1)q⁵ non-square-zero operators. Direct modular row-rank recomputation over all nonzero f in F2 and F3 gave stratum counts 32/24/7 and 486/216/26 and corresponding map totals 641 and 12758. No finite test is used as proof of the all-field statement. The theorem does not cover arbitrary-rank operators, conjugacy classes or scheme nilpotents.

originality.rationale: The surviving claim is the exact complete rank-one Nijenhuis fiber/kernel classification for the six-dimensional class-three Lie algebra of strictly upper-triangular 4x4 matrices, plus three distinct reduced incidence components and an all-field finite-field polynomial census. The Lie torsion identity itself is classical and is not counted as novel. The actual 2020 Lie representation paper proves compatible Kupershmidt/Nijenhuis constructions, the 2026 higher-Lie paper addresses L-infinity torsion over characteristic zero, and the 2026 low-dimensional classification addresses 2D pre-Lie and 3D associative products; their inspected statements do not entail the n4 fiber/census. A published finite-Lie-algebra rank-spectrum theorem concerns adjoint ranks on other filiform families. No exact n4 count/component theorem was identified in bounded Resultary and literature searches. Originality is best-of-knowledge, not comprehensive priority certification; the 2013 foundational paper full text remained inaccessible.

value.rationale: n4 is the first standard strictly upper-triangular matrix Lie algebra of nilpotency class three: its noncentral derived ideal distinguishes it from familiar two-step Heisenberg cases. The functionals form a natural projective flag stratification in their evaluations on the derived layers, and the exact jump in admissible image dimensions 1/3/6 yields three non-equidimensional geometric components. Both the component dimensions and the all-q rank-one census, including N²!=0 split, are natural deformation-geometric and arithmetic invariants a future researcher could use to compare Nijenhuis varieties across nilpotency classes/characteristics. This is neither a parameter renaming nor an arbitrary tiny numerical slice; it is a complete self-contained classification of a canonical rank-one locus. It makes no unsupported claim of a general arbitrary-rank theorem.

limitations: Classifies vector-space rank exactly one (plus the zero cone point), not arbitrary-rank Nijenhuis operators, conjugacy orbits or possible nonreduced scheme structure.
The finite modular tests are corroboration of the symbolic proof, not extrapolation to arbitrary fields.
Originality is best-of-knowledge with a documented inaccessible foundational 2013 paper and possible unfamiliar alias/general theorem; the original PDF was not claimed to have been read.
